layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Accurate segmentation of tubular, network-like struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures, such as vessels, neurons, or roads, is relevant to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: many fields of research. For such structures, the topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is their most important characteristic; particularly preserv-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing connectedness: in the case of vascular networks, miss-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing a connected vessel entirely alters the blood-flow dynam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ics. We introduce a novel similarity measure termed center-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lineDice (short clDice), which is calculated on the inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: section of the segmentation masks and their (morpholog-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ical) skeleta. We theoretically prove that clDice guaran-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tees topology preservation up to homotopy equivalence for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: binary 2D and 3D segmentation. Extending this, we pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pose a computationally efficient, differentiable loss func-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion (soft-clDice) for training arbitrary neural segmenta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion networks. We benchmark the soft-clDice loss on five

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: public datasets, including vessels, roads and neurons (2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 3D). Training on soft-clDice leads to segmentation with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more accurate connectivity information, higher graph simi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: larity, and better volumetric scores.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segmentation of tubular and curvilinear structures is an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: essential problem in numerous domains, such as clinical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and biological applications (blood vessel and neuron seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation from microscopic, optoacoustic, or radiology im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ages), remote sensing applications (road network segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation from satellite images) and industrial quality control,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: etc. In the aforementioned domains, a topologically accu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rate segmentation is necessary to guarantee error-free down-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stream tasks, such as computational hemodynamics, route

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: planning, Alzheimer's disease prediction [18], or stroke

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: modeling [20]. When optimizing computational algorithms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for segmenting curvilinear structures, the two most com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: monly used categories of quantitative performance mea-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sures for evaluating segmentation accuracy of tubular struc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plex, whole brain vascular dataset [48], where an exemplary 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: slice of the data is chosen and segmented by two different models,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: see purple (middle) and red (right), respectively. The two segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on the other side, the red segmentation captures all vessels in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image while being less accurate on the radius of the large vessel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Skeleta are drawn in yellow. From a topology or network perspec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tive, the red segmentation is evidently preferred.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tures, are 1) overlap based measures such as Dice, preci-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion, recall, and Jaccard index; and 2) volumetric distance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: measures such as the Hausdorff and Mahalanobis distance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, in most segmentation problems, where the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: object of interest is 1) locally a tubular structure and 2)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: globally forms a network, the most important characteris-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tic is the connectivity of the global network topology. Note

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that network in this context implies a physically connected

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structure, such as a vessel network, a road network, etc.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which is also the primary structure of interest for the given

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: *The authors contributed equally to the work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image data. As an example, one can refer to brain vascula-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture analysis, where a missed vessel segment in the segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation mask can pathologically be interpreted as a stroke

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: or may lead to dramatic changes in a global simulation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of blood flow. On the other hand, limited over- or under-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation of vessel radius can be tolerated, because it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: does not affect clinical diagnosis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For evaluating segmentations in such tubular-network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures, traditional volume-based performance indices

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are sub-optimal. For example, Dice and Jaccard rely on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the average voxel-wise hit or miss prediction [46]. In a task

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like network-topology extraction, a spatially contiguous se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quence of correct voxel prediction is more meaningful than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a spurious correct prediction. This ambiguity is relevant for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects of interest, which are of the same thickness as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution of the signal. For them, it is evident that a single-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: voxel shift in the prediction can change the topology of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whole network. Further, a globally averaged metric does

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: not equally weight tubular-structures with large, medium,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and small radii (cf. Fig 1). In real vessel datasets, where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vessels of wide radius ranges exist, e.g. 30 µm for arteri-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: oles and 5 µm for capillaries [48, 9], training on a globally

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: averaged loss induces a strong bias towards the volumet-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ric segmentation of large vessels. Both scenarios are pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nounced in imaging modalities, such as fluorescence mi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: croscopy [48, 58] and optoacoustics, which focus on map-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ping small capillary structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To this end, we are interested in a topology-aware image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, eventually enabling a correct network extrac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. Therefore, we ask the following research questions:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Q1. What is a good pixelwise measure to benchmark seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation algorithms for tubular, and related linear

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and curvilinear structure segmentation while guaran-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teeing the preservation of the network-topology?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Q2. Can we use this improved measure as a loss function

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for neural networks, which is a void in existing litera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture?

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.1. Related Literature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Achieving topology preservation can be crucial to ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tain meaningful segmentation, particularly for elongated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and connected shapes, e.g. vascular structures or roads.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, analyzing preservation of topology while simpli-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fying geometries is a difficult analytical and computational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem [11, 10].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For binary geometries, various algorithms based on thin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ning and medial surfaces have been proven to be topology-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preserving according to varying definitions of topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [23, 25, 26, 35]. For non-binary geometries, existing meth-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ods applied topology and connectivity constraints onto vari-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ational and Markov random field-based methods: tree shape

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: priors for vessel segmentation [44], graph representation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: priors to natural images [2], higher-order cliques which con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nect superpixels [53] and adversarial learning for road seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation [51], integer programming to general curvilin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ear structures [49], and proposed a tree-structured convolu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional gated recurrent unit [22], morphological optimization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Further, topological priors of containment were applied to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: histology scans [5], a 3D CNN with graph refinement was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used to improve airway connectivity [19], and recently,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mosinska et al. trained networks which perform segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation and path classification simultaneously [30]. Another

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach enables the predefinition of Betti numbers and en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forces them on the training[8].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The aforementioned literature has advanced the com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: munities understanding of topology-preservation, but crit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ically, they do not possess end-to-end loss functions that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: optimize topology-preservation. In this context, the litera-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ture remains sparse. Recently, Mosinska et al. suggested

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that pixel-wise loss-functions are unsuitable and used se-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lected filter responses from a VGG19 network as an addi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional penalty [29]. Nonetheless, their approach does not

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: prove topology preservation. Importantly, Hu et al. pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: posed the first continuous-valued loss function based on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Betti number and persistent homology [17]. However, this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method is based on matching critical points, which, accord-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing to the authors makes the training very expensive and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: error-prone for real image-sized patches [17]. While this is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: already limiting for a translation to large real world data set,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: we find that none of these approaches have been extended

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to three dimensional (3D) data.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.2. Our Contributions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The objective of this paper is to identify an efficient,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general, and intuitive loss function that enables topology

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preservation while segmenting tubular objects. We intro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duce a novel connectivity-aware similarity measure named

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clDice for benchmarking tubular-segmentation algorithms.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Importantly, we provide theoretical guarantees for the topo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: logical correctness of the clDice for binary 2D and 3D seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation. As a consequence of its formulation based on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: morphological skeletons, our measure pronounces the net-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work's topology instead of equally weighting every voxel.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Using a differentiable soft-skeletonization, we show that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: clDice measure can be used to train neural networks. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: show experimental results for various 2D and 3D network

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation tasks to demonstrate the practical applicabil-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity of our proposed similarity measure and loss function.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Let's Emphasize Connectivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intersecting skeletons with masks. We call this metric cen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: terlineDice or clDice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Topological Guarantees for clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The following section provides general theoretical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guarantees for the preservation of topological properties

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieved by optimizing clDice under mild conditions on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input. Roughly, these conditions state that the object of in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: terest is embedded in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in a non-knotted way, as is typi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cally the case for blood vessel and road structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Specifically, we assume that both ground truth and pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diction admit foreground and background skeleta, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: means that both foreground and background are homotopy-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equivalent to topological graphs, which we assume to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: embedded as skeleta. Here, the voxel grid is considered as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a cubical complex, consisting of elementary cubes of di-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mensions 0, 1, 2, and 3. This is a special case of a cell

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: complex (specifically, a CW complex), which is a space con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structed inductively, starting with isolated points (0-cells),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and gluing a collection of topological balls of dimension k

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (called k-cells) along their boundary spheres to a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dimensional complex. The voxel grid, seen as a cell com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plex in this sense, can be completed to an ambient complex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by attaching a sin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gle exterior cell to the boundary. In order to consider fore-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground and background of a binary image as complemen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tary subspaces, the foreground is now assumed to be the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: union of closed unit cubes in the voxel grid, corresponding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to voxels with value 1; and the background is the comple-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment in the ambient complex. This convention is commonly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: used in digital topology [24, 23]. The assumption on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background can then be replaced by a convenient equiva-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lent condition, stating that the foreground is also homotopy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equivalent to a subcomplex obtained from the ambient com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plex by only removing 3-cells and 2-cells. Such a subcom-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plex is then clearly homotopy-equivalent to the complement

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of a 1-complex.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 4.1. Soft-clDice using Soft-skeletonization:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Extracting accurate skeletons is essential to our method.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For this task, a multitude of approaches has been proposed.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, most of them are not fully differentiable and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: therefore unsuited to be used in a loss function. Popular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches use the Euclidean distance transform or utilize

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: repeated morphological thinning. Euclidean distance trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: form has been used on multiple occasions [42, 55], but re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mains a discrete operation and, to the best of our knowl-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: edge, an end-to-end differentiable approximation remains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to be developed, preventing the use in a loss function for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training neural networks. On the contrary, morphological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thinning is a sequence of dilation and erosion operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [c.f. Fig. 3].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Importantly, thinning using morphological operations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (skeletonization) on curvilinear structures can be topology-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preserving [35]. Min- and max filters are commonly used as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the grey-scale alternative of morphological dilation and ero-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion. Motivated by this, we propose ‘soft-skeletonization',

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where an iterative min- and max-pooling is applied as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proxy for morphological erosion and dilation. The Algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: putation. The hyper-parameter k involved in its computa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion represents the iterations and has to be greater than or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equal to the maximum observed radius. In our experiments,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this parameter depends on the dataset. For example, it is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in our experiments, matching the pixel radius of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our findings hold for the different network architectures,

layout_dets.text: 6. Conclusive Remarks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We introduce clDice, a novel topology-preserving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: similarity measure for tubular structure segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Importantly, we present a theoretical guarantee that clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enforces topology preservation up to homotopy equiva-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lence. Next, we use a differentiable version of the clDice,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: soft-clDice, in a loss function, to train state-of-the-art 2D

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and 3D neural networks. We use clDice to benchmark

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation quality from a topology-preserving per-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spective along with multiple volumetric, topological, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: graph-based measures. We find that training on soft-clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: leads to segmentations with more accurate connectivity

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: information, better graph-similarity, better Euler character-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: istics, and improved Dice and Accuracy. Our soft-clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is computationally efficient and can be readily deployed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to any other deep learning-based segmentation tasks such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as neuron segmentation in biomedical imaging, crack

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: detection in industrial quality control, or remote sensing.
